findings.quote: The scenarios weight to a fair value of $21.00, an expected upside of about 3.6% from the current price, against a bear case 26% lower, so the reward-to-risk near 0.14x does not compensate for the downside.
findings.issue: This restates, in near-identical words, sections.valuation.scenarioCommentary ("The scenarios weight to a fair value of $21.00, an expected upside of roughly 3.6% over the current price. The bear case sits 26% below the current price, so the reward-to-risk is skewed to the downside at about 0.14x"). The same load-bearing derivation (fair value $21.00, ~3.6% upside, bear 26% below, reward/risk ~0.14x) appears twice. The recurring-figure paraphrase also shows elsewhere: the WTI pair $95.65 vs $64.57 is stated numerically in four places (executiveSummary.risks[1], businessMoat.moatFactors[3].body, valuation.scenarios[2].driver, risks.idiosyncratic[2]) and the 72.4x/45.7x multiple pair across executiveSummary, valuation.multiplesCommentary, risks.idiosyncratic[0] and finalRecommendation, rather than being referred back in words.
findings.fix: Introduce the weighted fair value, expected upside, bear downside and reward/risk once (in scenarioCommentary); have the final recommendation refer back in words (e.g. "the scenarios above imply a HOLD; the reward/risk does not compensate") without re-stating the four numbers. Likewise state the WTI pair and the trailing multiples numerically once per topic and refer back thereafter.
findings.note: Consolidated to one home each with word-pointers elsewhere. Scenario derivation ($21.00/3.6%/26%/0.14x) now only in scenarioCommentary; finalRecommendation.body[1] refers back in words ("only slim expected upside against a materially larger bear-case downside"), no numbers. WTI $95.65/$64.57 numeric only in executiveSummary.risks[1]; moatFactors[3], scenarios[2].driver, idiosyncratic[2] now word-only. 72.4x/45.7x numeric only in multiplesCommentary; idiosyncratic[0] and finalRecommendation point back in words. Derivations recompute correctly; no invented figures.

findings.quote: The quarter's activity was supported by an oil-price spike, average WTI of $95.65, up from $64.57 a quarter earlier, that was tied to Middle East tensions and could unwind.
findings.issue: "Oil-price spike" is a characterisation the source does not use for a quarterly average, and the framing implies the WTI rise drove Select's Q2 activity. The MD&A stresses the opposite temper: activity "remained generally stable" with operators emphasising "capital efficiency" and "moderated production growth" even as prices rose, and the company attributes Q2 strength to produced-water volumes, skim oil, and record Chemical Technologies revenue. The causal link is only softly supported (MD&A: higher prices "supported the economics of ongoing development programs"), so this is a voice/emphasis overstatement rather than an ungrounded claim.
findings.fix: Drop "spike" and describe it plainly as the rise in average WTI to $95.65 from $64.57; frame the higher oil price as a supportive macro backdrop that could reverse, not as what drove the quarter's activity.
findings.note: Rewritten to "The quarter's average WTI rose to $95.65 from $64.57 a quarter earlier on Middle East tensions, a supportive macro backdrop rather than the driver of activity, which the MD&A describes as stable and capital-disciplined; that oil-price support could reverse." "Spike" is gone (no occurrence remains); the rise is now framed as a supportive backdrop, not the driver, and the MD&A's stable/capital-disciplined temper (Commodity Prices section) is cited. Grounded and matches the fix.
